bull_bear.body: Board recommended final dividend of Rs. 7 per share (350% on Rs. 2 face value) for FY26. Capital prioritized for working capital to support 30% order book growth and R&D for nuclear/data center specialized pumps.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical instability impacting gas availability and raw material costs (Strait of Hormuz reference). Jal Jeevan Mission funding delays at state level affecting dealer payments and dispatches. UK industrial sector weakness due to high energy prices reducing service demand. Execution risk on large nuclear/data center projects transitioning from prototype to commercial orders.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously Optimistic. Acknowledges transient operational headwinds (ERP, Labor Codes, JJM delays) but emphasizes strong order intake, pricing power via efficiency premiums, and strategic positioning in high-growth sectors (Nuclear, Data Centers). Conservative revenue recognition policy highlighted.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: KBL's US entry strategy via fire pumps (low service requirement) allowed distributor penetration where water pumps faced entrenched competition; now leveraging that footprint for high-margin data center cooling. Nuclear pump IP is fully indigenous (designed in India), reducing import dependency for critical atomic energy projects. 10 US states remain completely uncovered, offering latent geographic expansion.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet is run near debt-free: consolidated leverage of 0.1x in FY26 (0.3x in FY22), with net worth building from Rs 11,802 Mn in FY22 to Rs 24,759 Mn in FY26.
- A growing investment pool is held rather than deployed into leverage — investments including cash & cash equivalents and long-term investments other than in group companies rose from Rs 4,480 Mn at Mar-23 to Rs 10,716 Mn at Mar-26.
- The 1888–2020 history is framed as successive divestments (machine tools 1941, electricals and IC engines 1946, air compressors 1958) followed by an acquisition phase (SPP Pumps UK 2003, The Kolhapur Steel 2007, Braybar 2010, SyncroFlo 2014, Rodelta 2015); the 2021-onwards phase is labelled "Monetise".
- Strategy 2 is to "Monetize IPs" — out of 28 patents applied, 20 patents awarded (2 USA valid patents) — by expanding contribution from the services business and value-added products.
- Returns profile disclosed on a five-year view: RoCE of 11.8% (FY22), 21.3%, 26.4%, 27.0% and 19.3% (FY26); RoE of 8.0%, 16.8%, 22.3%, 21.9% and 16.5% (FY26).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Domestic: Growth in Building/Construction, Defense, Oil & Gas, Power (Thermal/Nuclear), Water/Irrigation. Retail segment hit by Jal Jeevan payment delays. International: US business (Rs. 540cr run-rate) diversified into Fire (35%), Data Centers (25%), and Municipal/Water. UK business faced EBITDA drop (Rs. 95cr to Rs. 58cr) due to high energy prices idling industrial service clients; pivoting to Water (United Utilities framework) and Data Centers.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as a "Global leader in turbomachinery and fluid management" and "India's 1st & largest pump manufacturer", with 138 years of engineering excellence; in 1926 KBL "created history by manufacturing and installing India's first indigenous centrifugal pump".
- Claims India's first and leading manufacturer of critical pumps for nuclear power plants, having supplied primary & secondary sodium pumps to Bhavini and specialised pump sets to the ITER project in France.
- Catering to 6 continents and 120+ countries, and states it provides drinking water to over 35% of India's population; active customer base 2,500+ across 20+ sectors.
- Frames its diversification as "Unimpacted by Cyclicality": segments span B2B, B2C and B2G and business models span Made to Stock, Made to Order, Engineered to Order, EPC and Services.
- Reference installations cited include The Shard (UK), Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge, Marina Bay Sands, Atal Tunnel, Statue of Unity, Sardar Sarovar and Thames River.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Merger] TKSL was merged into Karad Projects and Motors Ltd (KPML) with effect from 5th December 2025 per NCLT order dated 3rd November 2025; KPML figures include TKSL from Q3FY25 onwards, which affects comparability of the KPML series.
- [Board] Three independent directors — Mr. Shrinivas V. Dempo, Mr. Shobinder Duggal and Ms. Ramni Nirula — are shown as "Up to May 24, 2026", indicating a simultaneous board refresh.
- [Group structure] Kirloskar Brothers International B.V. (Netherlands, 100%) is the holding company/SPV for all international businesses; Kirloskar Ebara Pumps (45%) is a JV whose share of profit is consolidated, and Kirloskar Corrocoat is 65% held.
- [Order visibility] The deck frames the order book as the revenue-visibility anchor — "Robust Orderbook Implying Strong Revenue Visibility" — and notes pending order book excludes the small pump business, which is made-to-stock and executed from stock in the same month.
- [Recognition] Received the TPM excellence award from JIPM; SPP Pumps was awarded "Manufacturer of the Year" for the 4th consecutive year; the Kirloskarvadi pump testing laboratory achieved NABL accreditation and Hydraulic Institute accreditation.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: FY26 EBITDA margin compressed to 13.7% (vs higher historical levels) due to: 1) One-time Rs. 389mn labor code implementation cost (exceptional item); 2) Foundry ERP transition disruptions affecting small/medium pump dispatch; 3) UK mix shift from high-margin service to lower-margin product sales due to industrial idling from high power prices. Management expects margin recovery in FY27 as service work resumes and foundry efficiencies realize.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue: Targeting double-digit growth in FY27; Margin: Expect reversion to FY25 levels as UK service mix improves and foundry stabilizes; Order Inflow: Robust pipeline in Power, Water, Data Centers; Capex/Commissioning: Foundry ERP stabilization complete, focusing on operational efficiency rather than heavy greenfield capex.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Total consolidated order book stands at ~Rs. 39.5bn (Domestic Rs. 24.68bn + Intl Rs. 14.81bn). Domestic book grew 30% YoY driven by Building & Construction, Marine/Defense, Oil & Gas, and Power (Coal/Nuclear). International book grew 21% YoY fueled by Oil & Gas, Water utilities, and Data Centers in US/UK.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Nuclear Power: Indigenous IP for Fast Breeder and Small Modular Reactors (SMR) positions KBL for 100-200 GW nuclear target. Data Centers: High-value cooling/HVAC pump packages ($2mn+ per 1MW facility) with 25% contribution to US revenue already. Defense: Increased government focus on marine and defense pumping systems. Global EPC partnerships: Supplying Siemens, Alstom, Turkish contractors for overseas thermal projects.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: KBL delivered muted FY26 revenue (+1%) due to transient foundry ERP disruptions and Jal Jeevan funding delays, but Q4 momentum (+10%) and a record 30% domestic order book growth signal a strong FY27 rebound driven by nuclear indigenization and data center cooling demand. Margins faced headwinds from one-time labor code costs (Rs. 389mn) and a low-margin product mix in the UK, though management guides for margin recovery as service revenue normalizes.

open.horizon: FY26, as recommended by the Board
open.item: The Board has recommended a dividend of Rs 7 per equity share, i.e. 350% of the face value of Rs 2 each, for FY 2025-26 as per the Dividend Distribution Policy.

Management states the Group enters the new financial year with a strong and healthy order backlog providing positive visibility, and that the international business is well-positioned for sustained growth in the years ahead.
Capital expenditure will continue to be funded largely through internal accruals while adequate liquidity is maintained for present and future financial obligations.

Management expects growth in EBITDA and profitability driven by a stronger order book, a higher share of engineered and made-to-order products, easing commodity pressures and sustained contribution from services.
The Company will keep diversifying its revenue base through overseas services, IoT-enabled platforms and subscription-based offerings to enhance margins and earnings.
The Company will intensify initiatives that improve energy efficiency, reduce environmental impact and promote responsible resource management.

risks.note: Identified in the BRSR as both risk and opportunity: climate change can affect operations, supply chain continuity and cost structure through changing regulations, carbon reduction requirements and extreme weather events, implying increased compliance and transition costs; the offsetting opportunity is rising demand for energy-efficient pumping solutions.

Transition to a low-carbon economy may alter customer expectations, regulations and capital allocation. Negative implications flagged are capital expenditure required to transition to low-carbon operations, potential impairment of assets exposed to transition risks, increased compliance costs and potential loss of competitiveness if market expectations are not met. Mitigation is climate risk assessment, transition planning, sustainability targets and governance oversight.

A priority risk given industrial operations: manufacturing processes involving heavy equipment, welding, foundry activities and material handling require stringent safety measures. Negative implications include costs related to incidents, compensation, insurance, legal liabilities, operational downtime and regulatory penalties. Mitigation is EHS management systems, trainings, audits, incident investigation and safety culture.

Risks relate to waste generation and disposal and the associated social and regulatory impacts. Mitigation covers waste reduction initiatives, segregation and safe handling of hazardous and non-hazardous waste, recycling, reuse and recovery, strengthening circular economy practices and regular monitoring of waste generation and disposal.

The Board's Report describes FY 2025-26 as a global environment marked by slowing yet resilient economic growth, elevated energy prices and cautious capital spending - conditions that directly affect demand for capital equipment such as pumps.

Order momentum is described as coming from government bodies, OEMs and EPC contractors - the Water Resources Department Maharashtra, Kolkata Municipal Corporation, NVDA, the Government of Madhya Pradesh and the Uttar Pradesh Irrigation Department - so demand is structurally tied to government-led initiatives, urban infrastructure investment and industrial modernisation programmes.
risks.risk: Dependence on government-led and infrastructure spending

risks.note: Manufacture of fluid power equipment accounts for 94.30% of turnover, leaving the entity dependent on one product family, while exports contribute only 7.70% of turnover despite a presence in 120+ countries - concentrating standalone revenue in the Indian market.

Listed among the material topics identified in the report, alongside regulatory compliance and business ethics, as issues the Company tracks; no quantified exposure is disclosed in the routed sections.
